hints: Wes Anderson is an American filmmaker whose work blends comedy with melancholy.
His films feature carefully arranged compositions, distinctive colour palettes and meticulously designed fictional worlds.
He also makes stop-motion animation; recurring collaborators include actors Owen Wilson and Bill Murray.
Roald Dahl wrote imaginative fiction for children as well as stories for adults.
His young heroes often face cruel grown-ups, with mischief and unexpected twists shaping their adventures.
Quentin Blake illustrated many of his books, giving the strange creatures and exaggerated characters a distinctive appearance.
Stephen King is an American author strongly associated with horror and suspense.
His fiction often brings frightening events into recognisable communities and ordinary lives.
Maine is closely connected with his life and writing; his work also extends into fantasy and science fiction.
Dr. Seuss was the pen name of writer and illustrator Theodor Geisel.
His children’s books use rhythmic language, playful repetition and unusual invented creatures.
Many are designed for beginning readers, using a limited vocabulary with drawings that help carry the story.
William Shakespeare wrote for the English stage around the turn of the seventeenth century.
His drama spans comedy, tragedy and historical struggles for power.
The stories draw on royal chronicles, classical history and tales of love, mistaken identity and family conflict.
A protagonist is a central character whose choices and conflicts shape a story.
For Shakespeare, think of leading figures in stage dramas about love, ambition, family or political power.
His principal characters include rulers and ordinary people, and their stories range from comic misunderstandings to tragic consequences.
Christopher Nolan is a filmmaker known for large-scale thrillers and stories that test the viewer’s sense of reality.
His plots often rearrange time or explore memory, perception and difficult moral choices.
First-billed refers to the performer credited first in the cast, which is a narrower role than simply appearing in one of his films.
Steven Spielberg is an American filmmaker and the founder of Amblin Entertainment.
His career helped establish the modern blockbuster, pairing ambitious spectacle with accessible storytelling.
His work ranges from imaginative adventures to historical drama, often placing ordinary people in extraordinary circumstances.
Pixar is an animation studio that helped establish feature-length computer animation.
Its storytelling often gives human feelings and relationships to surprising kinds of protagonists.
Settings range from miniature communities underfoot to ocean journeys and fantastic workplaces connected to the human world.
Pixar creates animated stories using computer-generated imagery.
Its casts include people alongside creatures and objects given personalities and emotional lives.
Think of the inhabitants of miniature communities, ocean habitats and fantastic workplaces, including their families, allies and rivals.
DreamWorks Animation is a studio specialising in animated family entertainment.
Its stories often combine comic characters with fantasy, adventure or a surprising view of familiar worlds.
Think of comic fairy-tale reinventions, martial-arts adventures and unlikely friendships between people and fantastic creatures.
DreamWorks Animation creates family films and television stories.
Its worlds range from animal communities to fairy-tale settings and adventures involving fantastic creatures.
Look to fairy-tale communities, martial-arts training grounds and stories of young adventurers forming friendships with creatures others fear.
Studio Ghibli is a Japanese animation studio established in 1985.
The studio was created to make animated films by directors Hayao Miyazaki and Isao Takahata.
Its catalogue includes imaginative adventures and intimate human dramas, with detailed environments playing an important part in the storytelling.
James Bond is a fictional British secret agent created by novelist Ian Fleming.
The screen adventures combine espionage with international travel, dangerous opponents and elaborate action.
The official film series began in 1962 and continued across successive generations of leading performers.
James Bond is Ian Fleming’s fictional secret agent, also identified by the code number 007.
The official cinema series began in 1962 and has recast its central role across different eras.
This refers to the performer portraying the agent himself, rather than a supporting colleague or an opponent.
This fantasy series follows a hidden magical society alongside the ordinary world.
Much of the story centres on Hogwarts, a boarding school where young people learn magic.
The school has four houses, but the wider cast also includes relatives, officials and people on opposing sides of a larger conflict.
J. R. R. Tolkien’s fantasy is set in the imagined world of Middle-earth.
The story combines a long journey with a wider struggle over a dangerous source of power.
Its cast comes from different peoples and generations, and friendships are tested by war, responsibility and temptation.
This is the animated adventure series first broadcast by Nickelodeon in 2005.
Its world is divided into four nations associated with water, earth, fire and air.
Some inhabitants can control an element through movements resembling martial arts, while a long war shapes the characters’ journeys.
This is a crime drama created by Vince Gilligan.
The story begins with a chemistry teacher in New Mexico whose serious illness changes his plans for the future.
His entry into an illegal drug business draws family members, business associates and law enforcement into escalating conflict.
This series mixes science fiction, horror and a coming-of-age story.
The Duffer brothers set much of the action in the fictional town of Hawkins, Indiana, during the 1980s.
Young friends and the adults around them encounter secret experiments and threats connected to another dimension.
This HBO fantasy drama adapts the fiction of George R. R. Martin.
Much of the story concerns rival noble families seeking political control of Westeros.
Alliances, inheritance and divided loyalties shape the cast, while threats beyond court politics complicate the struggle.
This American sitcom presents an everyday workplace as though a documentary crew were filming it.
The setting is a paper company’s branch in Scranton, Pennsylvania.
Awkward management, coworker rivalries, practical jokes and relationships provide much of the comedy.
George Lucas created this space-fantasy setting for a film released in 1977.
The stories blend adventure and family conflict with struggles over the future of an entire galaxy.
Alongside spacecraft and advanced technology, a mysterious power called the Force connects the physical and spiritual sides of the setting.
This refers to the earliest group of creatures in the franchise’s creature-collecting world.
The original group is associated with the Kanto region and the beginning of the Pokédex numbering system.
The group contains related evolutionary stages as separate species, as well as creatures that have no evolution within that original set.
An alloy is a material formed by combining chemical elements while retaining metallic properties.
The ingredients include at least one metal, but another ingredient can be a non-metal.
Mixing changes useful properties such as hardness, resistance to corrosion or melting behaviour.
Subatomic physics studies matter at scales smaller than an atom.
Some particles are treated as fundamental, while others have smaller constituents inside them.
Physicists also study particles associated with interactions, rather than only those composing familiar everyday matter.
Geologists divide Earth’s long history into formally named intervals.
These intervals form a hierarchy, from the broadest spans down to more detailed subdivisions.
Boundaries are tied to evidence preserved in rocks, allowing researchers to relate events recorded in different places.
A metric prefix modifies the size of a measurement unit.
The internationally agreed prefixes represent multiplication or division by powers of ten.
They attach to a unit name or symbol, expressing very large or very small quantities without writing a long string of zeros.
Tom Hanks is an American performer whose career spans comedy and dramatic leading roles.
He is particularly associated with relatable people facing unusual pressure, responsibility or isolation.
His filmography spans romantic comedy, spaceflight stories, wartime experiences and survival drama, often balancing danger with moments of humour.
Harrison Ford is an American actor closely associated with adventure films and thrillers.
His screen persona often combines resourcefulness and dry humour with visible vulnerability under pressure.
His roles range from daring explorers and intelligence operatives to professionals drawn into dangerous investigations, alongside occasional romantic comedy.
Marsupials are mammals whose young are born at a very early stage of development.
The young continue growing while attached to the mother’s teats, often protected by a pouch.
They are especially associated with Australia, but many also live in the Americas; not every species has a fully enclosed pouch.
Legumes belong to the plant family Fabaceae, an important source of food crops.
The term is associated with the plants’ seeds and pod-like fruits; edible members can be harvested fresh or dried.
Many form partnerships with bacteria in their roots that make nitrogen available for growth, helping explain their importance in farming.
This musical family is identified by how the player starts the sound.
The player buzzes their lips into a mouthpiece, setting the air inside the instrument vibrating.
The tubing’s length and shape influence the range and tone, while changes in lip tension help select different notes.
A logical fallacy is a recurring error in reasoning that weakens an argument.
The problem lies in how the conclusion is supported, rather than simply whether the speaker’s claim happens to be true.
Check whether the evidence is relevant and sufficient, and whether the conclusion really follows from the reasons provided.
This concerns the relative masses of atoms, rather than the weight of a particular object.
Periodic tables report relative atomic mass, which differs from density: a small object can be light even when its material is dense.
The comparison point has a relative atomic mass of about 55.85; look to elements with a lower value.
A constellation is an officially defined region of the sky, associated with a familiar pattern of stars.
These regions give astronomers a way to describe where an object appears in the sky.
Many names come from mythology or animals; a familiar star pattern can also be an informal grouping rather than an official constellation.
NASA’s shuttle programme used winged spacecraft designed for repeated journeys to orbit.
The orbiter was the crew-carrying vehicle, launched with an external fuel tank and rocket boosters.
The fleet flew from 1981 to 2011, carrying out research, handling satellites and helping construct the International Space Station.
Jane Austen wrote English fiction that closely observes the society around its characters.
Courtship and marriage are tied to questions of money, status, family obligations and women’s independence.
Her social criticism often works through irony, exposing the distance between a character’s confidence and their understanding of other people.
This refers to the central traveller in the British science-fiction series Doctor Who.
The character journeys through space and time aboard the TARDIS, encountering different worlds with travelling companions.
Regeneration allows the character’s appearance and personality to change, so successive performers portray different incarnations.
Apollo was NASA’s effort to send people to the Moon and bring them safely back to Earth.
A landing used a separate lunar module for two crew members, while a third remained in lunar orbit.
Neil Armstrong led the first landing; later crews included Charles Conrad and Gene Cernan. Recall the mission number attached to a landing crew.
Mercury was the United States’ first human-spaceflight project; this asks for the people chosen at its beginning.
NASA selected these men from military test pilots after demanding medical, physical and psychological screenings.
The group included the first American in space and the first American to orbit Earth; several later flew in Gemini or Apollo.
